meta.description: Creates RNA-seq sashimi plots with ggsashimi, rmats2sashimiplot, leafviz, Jutils, and pyGenomeTracks, selecting the route by upstream splicing result and publication or interactive goal.
meta.audit_kind: final-pass re-audit at the pushed source tip; previous canonical report/viewer archived under _pre-fix-20260923 before this run
meta.inputs_note: Nine isolated, PID-owned executions used a source copy in run/phase2_final_0663f11_pid_owned_20260923. MAJIQ/VOILA remains explicitly licence-gated and was not executed; no claim of its runtime behaviour is made.
meta.env: F:/OpenScience/audit-envs/alternative-splicing; WSL science; as-viz-gg34 (R 4.2.3, ggplot2 3.4.4), as-rleaf, as-core; ggsashimi 1.1.5, rmats2sashimiplot 4.0.0, leafcutter 0.2.9, Jutils, pyGenomeTracks 3.9, regtools 1.0.0
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All reported output facts are from this run's logs or generated files. MAJIQ/VOILA is described as licence-gated rather than asserted to work.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill visualizes RNA-seq splicing evidence and does not provide diagnostic, therapeutic, or prescriptive conclusions.

methodological_ground.detail: The run exercised grouped BAM overlays, rMATS event plotting, leafcutter visualization preparation, result conversion, and coverage/junction tracks using real local fixture inputs.

code_usability.detail: Every shipped executable path was freshly exercised from a copied source tree: example functions, rmats2sashimiplot, leafviz build mode, Jutils pipeline and its four converters, and pyGenomeTracks preparation/rendering. The MAJIQ/VOILA reference is a documented licence boundary, not runnable evidence.

functional_suitability.note: Clear tool selection across major upstream splicing formats and rendering goals; the MAJIQ/VOILA path is necessarily unverified without a licence.

reliability.note: The example rejects missing BAMs, unknown contigs and empty regions; shell helpers use strict mode and check non-empty outputs where silent success is known.

performance_context.note: The comprehensive single Skill is useful but long; tool-specific references provide only partial progressive disclosure.

agent_usability.note: Inputs, flags, version notes, expected files and failure modes are concrete; several recipes rely on installed tools or prior block state.

human_usability.note: Decision guidance and command-oriented recipes make the intended route understandable to a working analyst.

security.note: No credentials or remote write actions; list-form Python subprocesses and sanitized plot names help. Shell recipes still accept user paths.

maintainability.note: Versions and compatibility constraints are named, but reproducible fixtures and automated tests are not shipped with the Skill.

agent_specific.note: Strong failure semantics, explicit licence boundary, version pin and postcondition language; the multi-tool scope remains cognitively dense.

key_strengths: Fresh PID-owned tests covered every non-licence-gated executable route from a copied source tree.
Input guards prevent ggsashimi from silently accepting missing BAMs or unknown contigs.
rMATS, leafcutter, Jutils and pyGenomeTracks all produced asserted output artifacts.

recommendations.title: Provide reproducible fixtures
recommendations.problem: The Skill itself has no small test fixture bundle.
recommendations.root_cause: The runnable recipes assume user-provided BAM, event, annotation, and index inputs, while the small deterministic fixtures exist only in audit infrastructure.
recommendations.fix: Add optional tiny fixtures and a smoke-test recipe so compatibility can be checked without audit infrastructure.

recommendations.title: Clarify recipe state
recommendations.problem: Some later examples presume files created by earlier blocks or a tool on PATH.
recommendations.root_cause: Prerequisite artifacts and PATH dependencies are described at workflow level rather than repeated beside each independently runnable block.
recommendations.fix: State dependencies adjacent to every runnable block.
